properties.displayName: [WEEKLY] Public-Facing App Runtime Spawns Shell, LOLBin, or Container-Control Tool
properties.description:
Detects an internet-facing application runtime — Node.js, Python/Jupyter, PHP-FPM, IIS w3wp, nginx, httpd, caddy, ruby, or java — spawning a shell, LOLBin, or container-control binary, optionally with a recon/privilege-escalation keyword in the child command line. This is the common post-condition shared across the fortnight's CRITICAL/KEV catch: PAN-OS GlobalProtect auth bypass under active exploitation (CISA KEV CVE-2026-0257; The Hacker News follow-up), three independent vm2 sandbox escapes (CVE-2026-47137 patch bypass, CVE-2026-47140 NodeVM denylist bypass, CVE-2026-47210 JSPI Promise species bypass), the Jupyter Enterprise Gateway KERNEL_UID/GID enforcement bypass (CVE-2026-44180), and the Shopper RBAC authorization bypass (CVE-2026-47744). Every one of these CVEs lets an unauthenticated/low-privileged HTTP touch defeat an auth/authz/sandbox check; the only host-visible signal the bypasses share is the privilege-boundary crossing that follows — a web/app process suddenly executing a shell, container-control tool, or LOLBin. The query spans the exploit and install stages by joining a parent in the app-runtime set to a child in the shell/LOLBin/container-control set on the same host. It fires when the bypass is converted to host action and does NOT fire on benign in-runtime behaviour (a Node API calling git, a PHP composer install, a Python wheel build invoking gcc) because none of those children are in the suspicious-child set; CI build agents and DevOps tooling running as app runtimes are the main FP source and should be allowlisted by hostname.

Rationale: Across the seven articles the only shared host-visible signal is the privilege-boundary crossing that follows the auth/authz/sandbox bypass: a web/app runtime suddenly running a shell, LOLBin, or container-control tool. Pivoting on the parent⇄child pair (instead of any single vm2/PAN-OS/Jupyter/Shopper IOC) catches the joint pattern and survives IOC rotation.
properties.query:
let AppRuntimes = dynamic(["node.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","jupyter.exe","php-fpm.exe","php.exe","w3wp.exe","nginx.exe","httpd.exe","caddy.exe","ruby.exe","java.exe"]);
let SuspChildren = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe","wsl.exe","wmic.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","kubectl.exe","docker.exe"]);
let ReconRegex = @"(?i)(whoami|\bid\b|uname|hostname|ipconfig|ifconfig|/etc/passwd|/etc/shadow|\bnet user\b|\bnet group\b|child_process|execSync)";
let PrivRegex  = @"(?i)(--privileged|runAsUser=0|runAsGroup=0|KERNEL_UID=0|KERNEL_GID=0|\b-uid\s+0\b|\b-gid\s+0\b|setuid\(0\))";
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ParentName = tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| extend ChildName  = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where ParentName in (AppRuntimes)
| where ChildName in (SuspChildren)
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| extend HasRecon = CommandLine matches regex ReconRegex
| extend HasPrivEscalation = CommandLine matches regex PrivRegex
| extend ScriptingRuntimeParent = ParentName in ("node.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","jupyter.exe")
| where HasRecon or HasPrivEscalation or ScriptingRuntimeParent
| summarize EventCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Cmds=make_set(CommandLine, 10), Users=make_set(SubjectUserName, 5) by Computer, ParentName, ChildName, HasRecon, HasPrivEscalation
| order by LastSeen desc
